---
title: "Troubleshooting"
---

Common problems when running rendehR on MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, eICU and their
demos, with the message you see, the cause and the fix. Code below is not
evaluated.

## Connections and credentials

### Where credentials come from

PostgreSQL settings are resolved field by field by `load_credentials()`: the
environment variables `PGHOST`, `PGPORT`, `PGUSER`, `PGPASSWORD` and `PGSSLMODE`
win, then the `postgres` block of the credentials file, then the defaults
(`localhost`, `5432`, `postgres`, `prefer`). PhysioNet uses `PHYSIONET_USER` and
`PHYSIONET_PASS`, then the `physionet` block of the file. The file is
`database.credentials_path` of the active project config, otherwise
`config/config_pass.json` in the working directory. Passing `creds =` to
`ehr_connect()` or `run_explorer()` bypasses the file; `download_source()` still
gives `PHYSIONET_USER` and `PHYSIONET_PASS` precedence over stored values.

```r
ehr_create_credentials_template("config/config_pass.json",
                                postgres_user = "postgres")
ehr_use_config("config/ehr_config.json")   # also clears cached credentials
ehr_connect()                              # or ehr_connect("rendehr", creds = load_credentials())
```

Credentials are cached for the session. After editing the file or the
environment variables, call `ehr_use_config()` again (or restart R).

### "PostgreSQL refused the password for user '...'"

The stored password is wrong. In an interactive session you are asked up to
three times; otherwise the call stops with
"Correct it in the credentials file (postgres$password) or PGPASSWORD."
Fix `postgres$password` in `config/config_pass.json` or set `PGPASSWORD`.

### "Connection refused" or "could not connect to server"

This error comes from the PostgreSQL client library and is passed through
unchanged: the server is not running, or `host`/`port` point to the wrong
place. Check the server (`pg_isready -h localhost -p 5432`), then the
`postgres` block or `PGHOST`/`PGPORT`. `ehr_connect()` only stores
credentials; the first query is where a connection error appears.

If you do not need PostgreSQL, run the supported stages on DuckDB:

```r
run_one_source("mimic_iv_demo", engine = "duckdb")
```

### "Retired PhysioNet environment variable(s) detected: ..."

`RICU_PHYSIONET_USER` / `RICU_PHYSIONET_PASS` are set. Rename them to
`PHYSIONET_USER` and `PHYSIONET_PASS`.

## Downloads

### "PhysioNet denied access to ..."

MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV and eICU are credentialed: you need a PhysioNet account
with approved access and the signed data use agreement for each dataset. The
open demos (`mimic_iii_demo`, `mimic_iv_demo`, `eicu_demo`) download without
credentials. In an interactive session a refusal prints
"PhysioNet refused these credentials, or the account has not signed the data
use agreement for this dataset." and asks again.

```r
download_source("mimic_iv_demo")                    # open, no credentials
Sys.setenv(PHYSIONET_USER = "me", PHYSIONET_PASS = "...")
download_source("mimic_iv", tables = c("patients", "admissions"))
```

### A download stopped part way

Run the same call again. Partial files are kept as `.part` files and resumed
("resuming from ..."); files already verified against `SHA256SUMS.txt` are
skipped. A file that does not match the manifest is reported and preserved,
not overwritten.

## Project configuration

### The wrong project config is used

When no config is loaded with `ehr_use_config()`, path helpers such as
`ehr_paths()` (used by every stage) load `EHR_CONFIG` or, if unset,
`config/ehr_config.json` relative to the working directory, and make it the
active config. A stray `config/` folder in the working directory therefore
wins over the defaults. Load the config explicitly and check what was resolved:

```r
ehr_use_config("~/projects/sepsis/config/ehr_config.json")
#> rendehR: project config loaded from '...'
ehr_config()$config_path
ehr_check_config(src_name = "mimic_iv")    # prints resolved paths and problems
```

`ehr_config_path()` is different: it returns the path of a file shipped with
the package (`inst/extdata`), not your project config.

### "Config file not found: config/ehr_config.json"

No config was passed and none exists in the working directory. Pass a path,
set `EHR_CONFIG`, or create one with `ehr_create_config_template()`.

## Memory, time and resuming

### Full data runs out of memory or takes hours

Cohort import always uses DuckDB. Give it limits and a spill directory, and
lower the chunk threshold for very large tables (MIMIC-III `chartevents`):

```r
run_one_source("mimic_iii",
  loading = loading_options(memory_limit = "24GB", threads = 8,
                            temp_directory = "/scratch/duckdb_tmp",
                            table_chunk_rows = 2e6))
```

The same arguments exist on `import_cohort_general()`. Adding the
`cache_raw_parquet` stage once avoids re-parsing compressed CSVs on later runs.
With `engine = "duckdb"` PostgreSQL is not used, but the PostgreSQL-only
stages (annotations, comorbidities, ISS, external concepts, harmonization) are
skipped. For a PostgreSQL bulk load, `loading_options(unlogged = TRUE,
set_logged = TRUE)` is faster.

### An import was interrupted

Run the same call again. If the selection and settings are unchanged you see
"Resuming an in-progress staging build from the last attempt." Chunks already
recorded as done are skipped; any chunk being written again is first deleted
from the staging table and re-inserted, so a kill mid-chunk leaves no
duplicates. If the settings changed, the message is "Discarding an
incompatible in-progress staging build ..." and the build starts fresh.

In `run_db()`, a table found partly loaded is reported as
"Resuming <table>: found n of m rows; truncating and reloading."

## Re-running stages

### "Current cohort is complete; no rebuild needed."

With the default `execution_options(overwrite = FALSE)`, `run_one_source()`
reuses a complete raw cache, cohort Parquet and loaded cohort tables. A
cohort built from a different selection stops with "The existing cohort
artifact at ... was built from a different cohort selection than this call
requests." An incomplete artifact stops with "The current cohort artifact is
incomplete or invalid". Rebuild, or use a separate `base_dir`:

```r
run_one_source("mimic_iv_demo", execution = execution_options(overwrite = TRUE))
run_one_source("mimic_iv_demo", stages = "run_concepts")   # one stage only
```

`overwrite` does not control whether concept SQL or harmonization rebuilds
their tables. Selected stages run in pipeline order; inputs of omitted stages
must already exist.

## Concepts and units

### "N problem(s) in the concept config for source '...'; rows with a skip problem are not built"

A row has an unknown or missing `itm_class` (allowed: `itm_itm`, `rgx_itm`,
`rgx_exp_itm`, `col_itm`) or an empty `match_value` for a class other than
`col_itm`. Check a file before running:

```r
validate_concept_config("config/my_concepts.csv", src_name = "mimic_iv")
```

### "`user_concepts` file not found: ..."

The path in `concept_options(user_concepts = ...)` does not exist relative to
the working directory. Use an absolute path. A user concept replaces every
shipped row with the same source and concept name.

### Values are NULL but the raw text is there

Values are parsed as numbers only when they look numeric; censored text such
as `<0.5` becomes `NULL`. With `conversion = "map"`, a unit missing from
`rendehr_concepts_unit_conversion_map.csv` that does not match the target
unit is also set to `NULL`. In both cases `value_raw` keeps the original
text. Add the unit and factor to the map to keep those values.

### Implausible values are still in the data

The pipeline does not drop out-of-range values. Range cleaning is opt-in:

```r
vitals <- clean_by_range(fetch_concepts("mimic_iv_demo", c("heart_rate", "resp_rate")),
                         src_name = "mimic_iv_demo", action = "na")
wide <- load_merged_ts_wide("rendehr_admission", spec, clean = "range")
```

`fetch_concepts_wide()` takes the same `clean = "range"`. Concepts without
bounds are listed with "clean = \"range\": no min/max bound for: ..." and
left unchanged.

## eICU specifics

### There are no dates

eICU stores offsets in minutes, not timestamps: window tables have
`admittime` 0, and `time_since_hadm_min` counts from the hospital admission
as in MIMIC. Cohorts are selected per ICU unit stay
(`patientunitstayid`), so a merged eICU admission holds only the selected
unit stays.

### Medication orders with a blank drug name

`run_raw_mods()` names them from `drughiclseqno` using the shipped
`rendehr_eicu_hicl_drugname_lookup.csv`. To use your own lookup (for
example one built from full eICU), put a file with the same name in the
project config directory; it replaces the shipped one. A missing file stops
with "Raw-mod lookup file not found: ...".

## Merged schema

### "... belong to a later ICU stay of the same admission; the admission-level merge keeps the first ICU stay."

At `analysis_level = "admission"` the merged `flat` and `cohort_info` hold
one row per admission, from its first ICU stay. For one row per ICU stay,
build the ICU timeline first and merge into a separate schema:

```r
make_icu_timeline("mimic_iv")
merge_sources(c("mimic_iv", "eicu"), target_schema = "rendehr_icu",
              analysis_level = "icu")
```

Without the timeline the merge stops with "Run make_icu_timeline(...) before
merge_sources(analysis_level = 'icu')."

## Explorer

`run_explorer()` serves individual-level data and listens on `127.0.0.1` by
default. Do not deploy it publicly or bind it to `0.0.0.0` on a shared
machine. Without stored credentials, an app built from a saved bundle runs
offline ("Offline (bundle only)"): pages that read the database live are
unavailable.

```r
d <- explorer_data("rendehr_admission", raw_dirs = c(mimic_iv = "data/source_data/mimic_iv"))
saveRDS(d, "bundle.rds")
shiny::runApp(explorer_app(readRDS("bundle.rds")))
```

The subject page's Verify check compares harmonized laboratory values with
the raw files. "No raw laboratory file or values found for this patient (raw
data directory not configured?)." means neither `raw_dirs` nor the paths
from `ehr_paths()` lead to the raw tables; pass `raw_dirs` to
`run_explorer()` or `explorer_data()`.

## Reporting a bug

Open an issue at <https://github.com/ATE-DRIVEN-lab/rendehR/issues> with the
source, backend, `packageVersion("rendehR")`, the call and the full message.
Never include credentials or patient-level data.
